scope: counted k=4 Gaudry solver (gaudry_quartic, chains+sparsest), p=29, 2 curves with full 2-torsion, 40 solves at Macaulay degree 29 (12 plain repeats, 12 transformed, 8 planted 3-point targets plain and transformed) + 6 Amendment-A1 transformed solves at degree 30-32; research/lift_dense_conjugate_pair_infinity_20261106
statement: On all 20 plain solves the quotient dimension is below 4096 exactly when the target is a sum of at most 3 factor-base points of the line (0 exceptions), on conjugate-pair and F_p lines alike. After a random projective change of coordinates (A in GL5(F_p)), 19 of 20 transformed solves succeed and return exactly the oracle's 4-point decompositions, including the 3/3 and 2/2 previously missed on curve 1; the failing one is a target that is itself a factor-base point (dimension 4130). Transformed cost is 0.970-1.030x the generic plain solve. On curve 1's two previously failing targets the transformed dimension stays at 4095 and 4094 at Macaulay degree 29-32.
